tips: Be specific: name the measure or intervention and the effect, rather than asking generally.
Phrase it as an effect or comparison question, e.g. "What effect does X have on Y?"
Use common, plain terms rather than jargon or unusual phrasing.
The example questions on the topics page are already checked — good as a template.

methodologyPage.heading: Methodology
methodologyPage.intro: How a TEKMESIS Evidence Report is built — step by step, transparent and traceable.

steps.title: Enter a question
steps.body: You pick a topic or write your own question.

steps.title: Refine the question
steps.body: TEKMESIS proposes a researchable phrasing, which you confirm or edit.

steps.title: Select data sources
steps.body: Depending on the topic, suitable scholarly databases are queried (see source routing).

steps.title: Search & screen studies
steps.body: Results are deduplicated, ranked by relevance and study design, and checked for eligibility.

steps.title: Assess eligibility
steps.body: Only sufficiently supported, comparable questions are offered as a report.

steps.title: Show the free teaser
steps.body: You see real search statistics, sources, and an initial orientation before you pay.

steps.title: Generate the full report
steps.body: After payment, the full structured evidence report is generated and validated.

privacyPage.heading: Privacy
privacyPage.intro: TEKMESIS is built to collect as little personal data as possible.

sections.title: No mandatory account
sections.body: You can use TEKMESIS without registering. Access to a paid report is via a secure, non-guessable link.

sections.title: Input warning
sections.body: Please do not enter names, documents, or confidential personal data. For health topics: no individual diagnoses, medication lists, or health records.

sections.title: Retention
sections.body: Unpaid drafts: 7 days. Paid reports: 12 months, then automatic deletion. You can request earlier deletion at any time.

sections.title: Link sharing
sections.body: Anyone with your report link can view the report. You can deactivate the link yourself at any time.

sections.title: No raw questions in analytics
sections.body: We record anonymized usage events (e.g. "report ready"), but never the raw text of your questions.

sections.title: Processors
sections.body: Payments via Stripe, transactional email via Resend, data storage via Supabase, analytics via PostHog (EU region).

aboutPage.heading: About TEKMESIS
aboutPage.body: TEKMESIS turns a question into an Evidence Report — real studies found, compared, and explained in plain language. With visible sources, honest limitations, and no false certainty.
aboutPage.whyTagline: TEKMESIS helps you quickly put everyday claims and questions to a scientific test — turning conflicting information into clear, evidence-based orientation.
whyParagraphs: TEKMESIS grew out of a simple observation: for many of life's important questions, scientific studies already exist — but for most people, they're hard to find, densely written, or seemingly contradictory.

At the same time, we increasingly run into fake news, misleading numbers, oversimplified claims, and statements that sound scientific but aren't. For non-experts, it's often nearly impossible to quickly tell what's actually backed by evidence, only partially plausible, or simply misrepresented.

That's exactly where TEKMESIS comes in. The platform helps you quickly and easily put personal questions, claims, and information to a scientific plausibility check. It finds relevant sources, compares studies, and transparently shows what's well supported, where results conflict, and what uncertainties remain.

I wanted to build something that helps people weigh information more soundly and make better decisions — whether the topic is learning, health, work, nutrition, technology, consumption, or anything else in everyday life.
TEKMESIS isn't meant to hand you neat, oversimplified truths. The goal is to make science understandable, and to draw a clear line between evidence, interpretation, and unsupported claims.
aboutPage.nameOriginBody: The name TEKMESIS originates from Ancient Greek and means proof, evidence, and reasoned conclusion. That's exactly what our platform stands for: we search, compare, and structure scientific findings so that complex studies become clear, traceable orientation.

glossaryDefinitions.meta_analysis: Statistically combines the results of multiple studies into one overall estimate — often considered particularly robust evidence when the underlying studies are themselves sound.
glossaryDefinitions.systematic_review: Searches systematically and by pre-defined rules for all relevant studies on a question and appraises them in a structured way — usually without a new statistical combination.
glossaryDefinitions.rct: Participants are randomly assigned to an intervention or a control group. This reduces the risk that systematic differences between groups distort the result.
glossaryDefinitions.quasi_experimental: Compares groups similarly to an RCT, but without true random assignment — making it more susceptible to biasing differences between groups.
glossaryDefinitions.cohort: Follows a group over time and compares how different exposures affect an outcome, without actively intervening.
glossaryDefinitions.case_control: Looks back at people with a given outcome and compares them to people without it, to identify possible contributing factors.
glossaryDefinitions.cross_sectional: Captures data at a single point in time. Shows possible associations, but no time sequence and therefore no statement about cause and effect.
glossaryDefinitions.case_report: Describes the observation in a single person or a very small case — a hint, not generalizable evidence.
glossaryDefinitions.review: Summarizes existing literature, usually without the pre-defined, systematic search method of a systematic review.
glossaryDefinitions.protocol: Describes a planned but not yet completed study — no results yet.
glossaryDefinitions.other: A study type that doesn't clearly fit any of the other categories.
glossaryDefinitions.unknown: The study type could not be determined from the available metadata.
glossaryDefinitions.evidence_certainty: How confident one can be, based on the overall body of evidence, that an observed effect is real and stable — not the same as "an effect exists or doesn't".
glossaryDefinitions.bias: A systematic distortion that can shift a study's result in a particular direction, independent of the true effect.

notResearchablePage.refineBody: Instead, ask about an effect, relationship, or difference — e.g. "What effect does X have on Y?".
